title: Paper-clay forest cabin ornament
subtitle: A small house ornament with a pointed roof, built from paper clay slabs
excerpt: A small forest cabin built from paper-clay slabs: four walls, a peaked roof, a scored door and window, and a chimney. Paper clay resists the thin roof panels cracking during drying. The finished piece is about 8 cm tall and hangs as a tree ornament or sits on a shelf.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Slab-building methods referenced from Encyclopedia Britannica 11th edition (1911) pottery entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: Air-dry clay mixed with cellulose fibres that strengthen thin sections and reduce cracking
A flat sheet of clay rolled to an even thickness, used as the building unit
The drying stage where clay holds its shape but is still damp enough to join pieces
Clay thinned with water, used as adhesive between clay pieces

. The cellulose fibres in the clay keep the thin roof panels from cracking. No kiln is needed.

materials.name: Small loop of cord or ribbon (for hanging)

content.text: Roll a slab 5 mm thick. Cut: two front/back walls 6 cm wide by 5 cm tall with a triangular gable above (cut the gable peak at 3 cm above the wall top, centred). Cut two side walls 5 cm wide by 5 cm tall. Cut two roof panels 7 cm wide by 5 cm long. Cut one chimney block 1.5 cm by 1.5 cm by 3 cm tall from a thicker piece of clay.

Score a door outline on one front wall with the needle tool: 2 cm wide by 3 cm tall. Score two small window squares on the side walls: 1.5 cm by 1.5 cm each. Score bark texture into the walls with horizontal lines if a log-cabin look is wanted.
Allow all pieces to firm to leather-hard before assembling (about 45 minutes).
to the edges. Assemble the four walls into a box shape, pressing and holding each corner join for a minute. Reinforce inside corners with small coils of soft clay.
Score and slip the top edge of each gable and the long edges of the roof panels. Press one roof panel down on each side so they meet at the roof ridge. Trim any overhang with a fettling knife.

Score and slip the chimney position on the roof. Press the chimney block in place near the ridge on the front side. Thread a cord loop through the chimney from the bottom before pressing it down if you want the cabin to hang.
Allow to dry flat over two to three days. Apply two coats of PVA. Paint with acrylic: white walls, brown roof, grey chimney. Add a dot of orange acrylic inside the chimney for a lit fire effect.
Make three cabins in graduated sizes for a village scene. Score a different pattern on each set of roof panels: tiles, shingles, or thatch lines.

items.problem: Roof panels crack along the ridge line during drying
items.cause: The two panels were joined at the ridge when still too soft and flexed as they dried
items.fix: Allow both panels to reach leather-hard before pressing them together at the ridge. Lay a thin rolled coil of soft clay along the inside of the ridge joint and smooth it in to reinforce

items.problem: Wall corners open up during drying
items.cause: The inside corner coils were too small to hold the walls square
items.fix: Apply fresh slip to the joint and press it together. Reinforce the inside corner with a larger coil of paper clay smoothed flat
